title: sharing: a predicate write asks one write verdict per candidate row, so a member bulk update over 10,000 rows owned by others costs ~5 s for no extra row; give ISharingService a bulk write-scope and verdict contract
body:
repo:objectstack#7 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibvVRcFWKrfWeG5jzPb

Filing gate ③. This is a follow-up from PR #35914 (card #35802), filed on the seat's 19:58Z call; the measurements are in os-dev report 7049211796. Dedupe: `ISharingService bulk`, `buildWriteFilter contract` and `writeVerdicts` returned no open card except #35802 itself.

## What happens
With #35914, a predicate (`multi: true`) update or delete composes the platform write floor per row, the way the by-id path does. Each matched readable row that the floor does not already admit costs one `ISharingService` `checkEdit` / `checkDelete` verdict, asked in batches of 25 and bounded by the existing 10,000 readable-row cap. That includes rows the sharing middleware's own `buildWriteFilter` will AND out anyway.

Measured on SQLite on the #35914 rig, with origin/main shown before the arrow:

| Case | Before → after | Reads | Rows written |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| (i) A member's predicate update over 1,000 readable rows owned by others; every verdict is `deny` | 44 ms → 1,085 ms | 3 → 2,004 | 0 |
| (ii) The same over 10,000 rows | 47 ms → 5,298 ms | 3 → 20,004 | 0 |
| (iii) A Modify All holder over 10,000 rows | 47 ms → 1,796 ms | 2 → 10,003 | 10,000, all of which the by-id path also admits |
| (iv) Under an authored `using` write policy | 0 verdicts asked (the S2 early return) | | |

On a networked database each read is a round trip, so the real cost is larger.

## Ask
Two parts, both additive to the `ISharingService` contract in `packages/spec`, so they need a contract decision:
1. **A bulk write scope** (for example `buildWriteFilter(object, ctx, verb)` exposed on `ISharingService`). plugin-security ANDs it into the candidate read, so only rows the sharing middleware would let through are asked about. This removes the member all-deny cost, cases (i) and (ii). It changes no row's answer, because a row outside that scope is ANDed out by the sharing middleware today.
2. **A bulk verdict** (for example `writeVerdicts(object, ids, verb, ctx)`) that answers the same tri-state as per-row `checkEdit` / `checkDelete`, with one owner-scope read, one share read and one Modify All check per batch. This cuts case (iii) from 1 read per row to about 3 reads per batch.

## Done when
- Both contract additions are made, with an equivalence pin showing each bulk verdict equals the per-row verdict on the #35914 matrix: owner, non-creator owner, creator non-owner, Modify All, edit share, queue member, and each delegated case.
- plugin-security uses both, and the #35914 pins stay green.
- The bench shows case (ii) back near the main baseline and case (iii) at or below 3 reads per 25-row batch.

## Business rationale
Flows, scheduled jobs and server-side bulk updates run predicate writes as business users. After #35914, a rep's bulk update over a shared org-readable object pays for one sharing verdict per row it can see, even when it can write only a handful. Today that is bounded by the 10,000 cap and named in #35914's changeset. A rep's bulk action over a large account list goes from milliseconds to seconds.

Reader: area:data, plugin-sharing and the spec contract owner. Grade, domain and queue are left to triage.
